parameters.name: min_samples_split
parameters.meaning: Minimum fraction of fitting samples required to split an internal node.

parameters.name: min_samples_leaf
parameters.meaning: Minimum fraction of fitting samples required in each leaf after a split.

parameters.name: min_weight_fraction_leaf
parameters.meaning: Minimum fraction of total fitting-sample weight required in a leaf.

parameters.name: max_features
parameters.meaning: Fraction of input features considered at each split.

parameters.name: min_impurity_decrease
parameters.meaning: Minimum weighted impurity decrease required for a split.

prior_facts: Floating-point min_samples_split and min_samples_leaf become sample-count thresholds through ceil(fraction * number of samples fitted in the fold).
Without sample_weight, samples start with equal weights. min_weight_fraction_leaf constrains the fraction of total sample weight in each leaf.

Floating-point max_features becomes max(1, int(max_features * n_features_in_)) features per split. Different inputs can select the same number of features. Finding a valid split may require inspecting more features than this number.
Depth, leaf size, minimum split size, and minimum impurity decrease jointly constrain tree growth.
background: Tune six hyperparameters of a random forest classifier on the Iris flower classification dataset to reduce cross-validation prediction error.
input_instructions: Submit all six hyperparameters using values within the parameter table bounds. max_depth is an integer; the other parameters are floating-point values.
The transform field describes search coordinates, not the submission format. For example, submit min_samples_leaf=0.1 directly, not its logit transform.
evaluation_details: The 150 samples are split into 120 training samples and 30 held-out samples, with four features per sample. Optimization feedback uses five-fold stratified cross-validation on the training split, without shuffling (shuffle=False).

Cross-validation error is 1 - mean fold accuracy. Minimizing this error is equivalent to maximizing mean accuracy. The run objective below specifies which metric the interface returns; held-out results are not optimization feedback.
The random forest uses 10 trees and random_state=0. Other fixed settings appear under fixed_estimator_parameters. No additional data preprocessing is applied.
